The test image shows a tomato stem cut longitudinally, revealing dark brown/black discoloration of the internal vascular tissue running along the length of the stem. The outer cortex remains green. This is classic vascular discoloration, pointing to a wilt/canker disease.

Top candidates: Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato, Verticillium_Wilt.

Let me view a reference for Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato:

The reference image for Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt shows leaf margin scorch symptoms, not the internal stem vascular discoloration shown in the test image. However, Bacterial Canker and Wilt is well-documented to cause dark brown-to-black vascular streaking when stems are cut longitudinally — exactly what the test image displays.

Key observations from the test image:
- **Stem cut longitudinally** revealing internal tissue
- **Dark brown to near-black discoloration** running through the vascular bundles
- Some external browning/cracking on the stem surface (left side)
- Outer green cortex relatively intact

This pattern of internal vascular discoloration is the hallmark diagnostic feature of **Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato** (*Clavibacter michiganensis* subsp. *michiganensis*), which causes dark streaking in the vascular system visible in stem cross-sections/longitudinal cuts. Verticillium Wilt is an alternative, but typically shows lighter tan-brown discoloration, not the deep dark streaking seen here.
